CampaignResponse.description:
A campaign as this API answers for one.

`public_url` is a plain string and not an `HttpUrl`: it is built from a domain name the
tracker gave us, and a response model that refused to serialise somebody else's data
would turn a campaign that exists into a 500.

setup_failure.description: Why this campaign's flows are missing, filled in by the call that has just tried to build them. A campaign read back later says `needs_attention` without it.
setup_failure.title: Setup Failure

CampaignResponse.title: CampaignResponse

CampaignSetupStatus.description:
How far part 1 got with this campaign.

The tracker cannot answer it: the campaign exists there either way, and only a flow
that was never created tells the two apart.
CampaignSetupStatus.title: CampaignSetupStatus

CampaignStatsResponse.description:
One campaign's numbers for one day, with everything needed to caption them.

A flow or an offer the report did not mention has no row at all, and that is deliberate:
a zero written here would be this service inventing a measurement. The screen draws an
empty cell, which is what "the tracker said nothing about this" looks like.

available.description: Whether these rows are the tracker's numbers at all. False is not an empty day: a campaign with no traffic is available with no rows.
available.title: Available

day.description: The tracker's day, not this service's.
day.title: Day

read_at.description: When the tracker answered, and null when it never has.
read_at.title: Read At

stale.description: These are the last numbers that could be read, not today's latest.
stale.title: Stale

timezone.description: The IANA zone `day` was worked out in.
timezone.title: Timezone

unavailable_reason.description: Why the last attempt failed, in words a buyer reads.
unavailable_reason.title: Unavailable Reason

CampaignStatsResponse.title: CampaignStatsResponse

CampaignsPageResponse.description: One page and the token that continues it, `null` meaning there is nothing after.
CampaignsPageResponse.title: CampaignsPageResponse

ConflictingState.description:
Two readings of one flow, side by side, in the same shape so they can be diffed.

Carried on the 409 a push answers when the flow has been edited in Keitaro meanwhile.
A body that only said "conflict" would leave the screen with nothing to show and the
person with nothing to decide between overwriting and discarding.
ConflictingState.title: ConflictingState

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Flow 1 catches this country and sends it away.
country.title: Country

name.description: What the campaign is called in the tracker.
name.title: Name

offer_id.description: The offer Flow 2 rotates, as the tracker numbers it.
offer_id.title: Offer Id

DraftDiffResponse.description:
What the draft would change, for a person and for the tracker.

`desired` is the exact payload a push sends, not a description of one: it is the same
tuple, rendered by the same function. That is what makes PREVIEW a rehearsal.
DraftDiffResponse.title: DraftDiffResponse

DraftOperationKind.description: The three edits the editor offers. Pinning is not among them: it changes no share.
DraftOperationKind.title: DraftOperationKind

DraftOperationRequest.description: One edit: what to do, and to which offer.

offer_id.description: The offer, as the tracker numbers it.
offer_id.title: Offer Id

DraftOperationRequest.title: DraftOperationRequest

EditDraftRequest.description: A batch of edits, applied in order and all or nothing.

operations.description: Applied in the order given. One the flow refuses rolls back the whole batch, so a request that answers 409 has changed nothing.
operations.title: Operations

EditDraftRequest.title: EditDraftRequest

ImportCampaignRequest.description: The one number that opens a campaign somebody else built.

keitaro_campaign_id.description: The campaign's id in Keitaro, as its URL shows it.
keitaro_campaign_id.title: Keitaro Campaign Id

ImportCampaignRequest.title: ImportCampaignRequest

InvalidField.description:
One field a request was refused over, and who refused it.

`location` is dotted from the outside in — `body.country`, `query.limit` — and a
complaint the *tracker* made about a field it was sent is prefixed `tracker.`, so that
one list can carry both without a client having to ask which kind it is holding.
InvalidField.title: InvalidField

OfferCatalogueSyncResponse.description:
What one press of the refresh did.

`synced_at` is `null` when the tracker listed no offers at all: the local copy was left
exactly as it was, because an empty answer and a failed listing are the same answer from
here and emptying a working catalogue is the worse of the two mistakes.

offers.description: How many offers the tracker listed.
offers.title: Offers

OfferCatalogueSyncResponse.title: OfferCatalogueSyncResponse

OfferResponse.description:
One catalogue offer, in the fields the reference tool's own label is made of.

`11112 Oxys [BEAUTY-CL-BE_0155] [pl es -]` — the id, the name, the network and the
countries, which is every field here and no others.

`country` is a tuple of plain strings and `preview_url` a plain `str`. Both are somebody
else's data: a dash is one of the values Keitaro really keeps in that array, and a
response model that refused to serialise what the tracker sent would turn an offer that
exists into a 500.
OfferResponse.title: OfferResponse

OfferShare.description: One offer row of a flow, in the three fields the tracker itself keeps.
OfferShare.title: OfferShare

OfferStatsResponse.description: What one offer did today — one cell of the editor's Stats column.
OfferStatsResponse.title: OfferStatsResponse

OffersResponse.description: A page of the combobox. No cursor: the catalogue is searched, not walked.
OffersResponse.title: OffersResponse

PinOfferRequest.description: The one number this API takes from a client, and it is still validated server-side.

share.description: Where to hold the row. Omitted means where it is now, which is the button as the screen offers it. Pinning recalculates nothing until the next edit.
share.title: Share

PinOfferRequest.title: PinOfferRequest

ProblemDetails.description:
A failure, as this API reports one.

Every member the RFC defines that this service fills in, plus the three that carry what
a screen does with a failure: the slug, the id to quote, and the campaign the problem is
about where there is one — which is what lets "already imported" offer to open the
campaign instead of only refusing the request.
ProblemDetails.title: ProblemDetails

PushDraftRequest.description: What the push may do about a flow somebody edited in Keitaro meanwhile.

overwrite.description: Push over changes made in the tracker since this draft was opened. The answer to a 409 and nothing else: overwriting another person's work is a decision.
overwrite.title: Overwrite

PushDraftRequest.title: PushDraftRequest

ReadinessResponse.description:
Body of `/readyz`.

`checks` maps a component name to its verdict and is empty at 1.6, which is the
honest answer: nothing this process depends on exists yet. 5.8 adds
`checks["database"]` and, with it, the 503 branch and the `503` entry in this
operation's OpenAPI responses — all three in one commit, and all before the frontend
generates its types from this schema at 9.6. The shape around `checks` does not move.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ShareChangeResponse.description: One offer's share, before and after — the `34 → 33` of the diff summary.
ShareChangeResponse.title: ShareChangeResponse

StreamFilterResponse.description: One condition on a flow — `country accept ["AU"]` in the reference campaign.
StreamFilterResponse.title: StreamFilterResponse

StreamResponse.description:
One flow: its heading, its rows already ordered, and whether PUSH may be pressed.

`absent` is a flow Keitaro has stopped returning. It is still drawn, because a flow that
vanished from the tracker is something to be told about rather than something to hide.

schema.description: `landings` is the only one that rotates offers. Flow 1 is a `redirect`.
schema.title: Schema

StreamResponse.title: StreamResponse

StreamRowResponse.description:
One line of the offer table.

`offer` is `null` for an offer the local catalogue has never heard of, which the screen
draws as `#11234 (not in catalogue)` rather than emptying itself. There is no foreign key
from a flow row to the catalogue and there is not meant to be.
StreamRowResponse.title: StreamRowResponse

StreamStatsResponse.description: What one flow took today — the number the editor prints in the group heading.
StreamStatsResponse.title: StreamStatsResponse

StreamsResponse.description: The whole editor screen: the campaign in the toolbar, and its flows below it.
StreamsResponse.title: StreamsResponse

Shared token.description: The value of ADROBOT_ACCESS_TOKEN, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

post.summary: Create a campaign with its two flows

get.description:
Two reports behind one answer, cached for the whole process for forty-five seconds.

No 502 in the list above, and that is the endpoint's contract rather than an oversight:
a report the tracker would not build comes back as `available: false` with a reason.
get.summary: Read this campaign's clicks today, by flow and by offer

get.description: Draw the whole screen in one answer: the mirror, the live draft over it, the pins.
get.summary: Read one campaign's flows as the editor draws them

delete.description: CANCEL. The pins survive it, and so do the tracker's own unnormalised shares.
delete.summary: Throw this flow's staged edits away

post.description: Apply a batch of edits. All or nothing: a refusal leaves the flow exactly as it was.
post.summary: Stage add, remove and bring back on this flow

get.summary: Show what pressing PUSH would send, without sending it

post.description: PUSH TO KT. A 409 carrying `conflict` means somebody edited the flow in Keitaro.
post.summary: Write this flow's draft to the tracker

delete.description: Release the pin if there is one. Silent when there is not: a second press is not an error.
delete.summary: Let one row back into the division

put.description: Pin a row. Deliberately moves no other share and lights no button — see the use case.
put.summary: Hold one row's share where it is

schema.title: Q

post.description: `synced_at` is null when the tracker listed nothing: the copy was left alone.
post.summary: Read the tracker's whole offer list again

get.description:
Answer 200 for as long as the process can serve a request.

Dependency-free on purpose: a liveness probe that touches the database turns a slow
query into a container restart loop.

Report whether this process is ready to take traffic.

At 1.6 it has nothing to ask: there is no database yet, and the tracker is not
allowed to be part of this verdict. It answers 200 with an empty `checks` rather than
inventing a component that cannot fail.
